findings.body: When the last task is merged through `forge merge`, completion is recorded in a `Forge-story-done` squash-message trailer (`src/forge/merge.py:88`), while the story JSON can remain `approved`. This row uses that JSON without consulting `story.completed`, so the machine board keeps a finished story marked approved and reports that its outcome still needs recording. The text view already resolves completion through `story.completed` (`src/forge/nextstep.py:358`), as does the HTML board (`src/forge/board.py:344–346`). Apply the same completion resolution here and cover the last-task merge through the JSON command.

findings.body: All three new test functions use `setup(repo)`, whose default is `forge-source` and which writes the currently running version directly into `forge.toml` (`tests/test_story.py:67–71`). None exercises the machine views in a newly initialized or adopted client repo, or in an existing client repo adopted on an earlier release and upgraded. The later one-line switch to `repo = "client"` only checks an unknown worker model. Add command coverage for both client lifecycles, including the earlier-release case required by the repository’s review rule.
